item.title: Trump “doubles down on data centers”
item.description: President Trump stated on Truth Social that Americans who oppose data centers are “backwards and poor”. Scott Galloway and Jessica Tarlov discuss, on Raging Moderates.

item.title: "Canadian consumers have something Americans don't."
item.description: Trump’s attempt to intimidate Canada and Prime Minister Mark Carney are destined to backfire — even if Canada might suffer in the short-term. It’s a betrayal of what’s made America work over the past 80 years, according to Scott Galloway and Jessica Tarlov on Raging Moderates.
item.content:encoded:
YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/K5vVXbacJxQ

Transcript

Canada's new counter tariffs are officially in effect despite escalating threats from Trump in recent days. He even floated the idea that he might end all trade with Canada. He also posted an image of him and Prime Minister Mark Carney as hockey players with Carney on the ice and Trump shouting, "Get up, Governor." >> 93, "Get up, Governor." Like, you kind of can't hate this guy enough. >> Yeah, look, one of them is a leader who acquits himself with dignity and grace and is befitting of his position. The other is Donald Trump. This is like a divorce where you live in the same town, go to the same church, and live in the same house. Like all tariffs, the person

who initiated it likely ends up on the losing end of this because Canadian consumers have something American consumers don't have and that is resolved. Canadians are rallied behind this. They are really upset and angry. They're going after the heart and lungs of some of these red states. >> I'm overwhelmed by the precision with which Canada is doing this and the slop factory that seems to be our trade apparatus at this point. We have no reporting that there has been anything

close to another round of negotiations or a deal. >> We don't cooperate with our allies. We're under the impression that we're the only part that matters and not recognizing the last 80 years our strength has come from a whole that's greater than the sum of its parts in terms of our alliances and democracies and being seen as the good guys. And to be clear, Canada has not grown their economy in 10 years. It is not a well-run economy. But the reason why they will ultimately win this trading war despite registering more pain is because they have the support of the

Canadian people.
